title: Police investigating ‘shameful’ Ibrox pitch invasion following Celtic’s win over Rangers
content:
Police Scotland says it will investigate the “shameful” scenes that followed Sunday’s Scottish Cup quarter-final between Rangers and Celtic at Ibrox Stadium.

Chief superintendent Kate Stephen confirmed in a statement that “a number” of arrests had been made, adding that officers and members of the public had been injured.

Celtic won the latest Old Firm derby on penalties following a goalless draw, with Tomas Cvancara scoring the winning spot kick in front of the home crowd, prompting some of the away fans at the opposite end of the ground to enter the pitch. Footage showed some supporters hugging and trying to take photos with Celtic players.

Rangers fans then also entered the pitch in greater numbers, some wearing blue masks. Police and stewards attempted to keep the two sets of supporters away from each other, with a line of officers forming on the edge of the penalty area in front of the Celtic fans.

Objects including pyrotechnics appeared to be thrown into the away end from Rangers supporters on the pitch. Pyrotechnics appeared to then be thrown from the section of Celtic fans back onto the pitch in the direction of the Rangers supporters.

After a few minutes, footage showed the Rangers fans running off the pitch and back into the stands.

The Scottish FA condemned the behaviour of the supporters who had entered the pitch and confirmed an investigation would be carried out in a statement shortly after full-time.

“The behaviour of a number of supporters at the Scottish Cup quarter-final between Rangers and Celtic at Ibrox today was shameful. It must be condemned by everyone involved in football and wider society,” Stephen said.

“A number of arrests have already been made, and Police Scotland will now work with both clubs and the Scottish Football Association to carry out a robust investigation following the scenes on the pitch at the conclusion of the match.

“Officers and stewards were faced with extreme hostility and violence over a sustained period, with many individuals having armed themselves with items clearly intended to cause harm. Officers and members of the public have been injured in this despicable display and I want to express my thanks to all officers and staff deployed.

“The investigation will also include the actions of some supporters who entered the Broomloan Road Stand without tickets before the match started, forcing delays in the security operation and the turnstiles to be closed for a period of time.”

Rangers head coach Danny Rohl appeared unaware of what happened when speaking to Premier Sports after the game. “I’m not sure what (it) was in the end, I was in the tunnel — I didn’t see anything,” he said.

“It looked as though there were a few tete-a-tetes, as much as anything else,” Celtic boss Martin O’Neill told the broadcaster. “It’s unfortunate, but hopefully it doesn’t dilute the importance, in terms of character.

“That may well be (the story of the match) and I need to have a think about it, at the end of the day. Old Firm games are explosive, they always have been, and maybe that’s one of the reasons why the derby’s one of the best in the world.”

Celtic’s Viljami Sinisalo added: “It’s a tough one. There’s no derby like it; it’s not going to take away from what we’ve done here today. We’ve come here, beat them and we’re into the next round of the cup. That’s the main thing we can focus on.”

Games between Rangers and Celtic are heavily policed and often lead to disturbances around the city of Glasgow, where both clubs are based.

Sunday’s game saw Celtic fans allocated the full Broomloan Road Stand at Ibrox for the first time since 2018, following years of reduced allocations for away supporters by both clubs, triggered by Rangers first doing so in December of that year.

Celtic issued a safety notice to their supporters on Friday, encouraging fans to arrive at Ibrox as early as possible and reiterating the ban on “fireworks, smoke bombs, firecrackers and all pyrotechnics”.
